message.reasoning:
I need to make a Monopoly decision.

I have $77 and am on Mediterranean Avenue after paying $250 rent. I own the pink and orange monopolies but New York is mortgaged. Player 2 has $540 and owns the Electric Company and a mortgaged North Carolina.

Player 3 has $397 and is in jail with hotels on Mediterranean and Baltic. Player 4 has $3251 and owns light blue hotels plus railroads. My cash is now only $77.

Baltic Avenue is one space away. A roll of 1 would cost $450 in rent. I must decide post-turn actions before ending this turn.

A roll of 1 is impossible, so I will not land on Baltic next turn. I will advance to Community Chest, then continue around the board.

Rolling a 2 lands on Baltic Avenue with its hotel, costing $450. That is a 2.8% chance of catastrophic loss with only $77 cash. Rolling a 5 or 6 would hit the light blue hotels at Oriental and Vermont for roughly $550 each.

Rolling a 3 would hit Income Tax for $200, which is also fatal with only $77. Rolling a 4 lands on the mortgaged Reading Railroad, so no rent is due. Rolling a 7 would hit the Connecticut hotel for roughly $600. Any roll of 8 or higher is safe.

Virginia is not a monopoly. Its rent is only $12, so landing there would be harmless.

Eighteen of thirty-six possible rolls are fatal. That is a fifty percent chance of immediate bankruptcy next turn.

Mortgaging properties would raise cash. St. Charles Place and States Avenue mortgage for seventy dollars each. St. James Place and Tennessee Avenue mortgage for ninety dollars each. Water Works mortgages for seventy-five dollars. Marvin Gardens mortgages for one hundred forty dollars.

Mortgaging all properties would raise cash to six hundred twelve dollars. That covers every dangerous roll with a small remainder left over. The engine only allows one mortgage per action, so I should start mortgaging now rather than waiting for debt.

I cannot wait for a debt to arise. With only seventy-seven dollars, no mortgage would cover a fatal roll. I will mortgage properties now rather than waiting.

Mortgaged properties stop collecting rent. I am checking standard rent values for my pink and orange monopolies to weigh the income loss against the bankruptcy risk.

Standard mortgage values are confirmed. I am now questioning whether the engine allows mortgaging during debt resolution, since the prior strategy assumed cash plus mortgage value could cover a hit.

The engine allows mortgaging during debt resolution. Pre-mortgaging is unnecessary and harmful. It would lose rent income, add ten percent interest later, and signal desperation to opponents. I will end this turn now and mortgage only if a debt actually arises.

I am now weighing a trade. Player 4 has $3,251 and light blue hotels, but his monopolies are incomplete. He lacks Marvin Gardens for the light blue set and St. Charles Place and States Avenue for the pink set. I have those missing pieces. I am checking whether he also owns Pennsylvania Avenue to see if he has an incomplete green monopoly.

Player 4 owns Pennsylvania and Kentucky, so the green and red monopolies are split. Player 3 has Indiana and Illinois mortgaged, while Player 4 has Kentucky alone. I have all three orange properties, but New York is mortgaged and cannot be unmortgaged now because I lack the one hundred ten dollars required.

I cannot build houses on the orange monopoly because I lack the cash. Player 4 is winning badly, but my orange set could pressure him if I ever had enough money to develop it. Player 3 has dark blue and brown hotels and is in jail with $397. I am considering a trade with Player 4, but selling Marvin Gardens would complete his yellow monopoly and strengthen the leader.

I am now considering trading with Player 2 or Player 3 to raise cash for unmortgaging New York and building houses. I am checking what each opponent wants.

Player 3 needs Kentucky from Player 4 to complete the red monopoly. Player 2 has $540 cash but owns almost nothing of value. I am considering offering Water Works to Player 2 in exchange for cash, since it pairs with their Electric Company.

Player 2 would not pay enough for Water Works to cover the full cost of unmortgaging New York and building houses. Even a large offer from Player 2 would leave me short of the cash needed to develop the orange monopoly.

Developing the orange monopoly into hotels would cost roughly $1,600, which is impossible from my current cash position. The practical strategy is to survive and hold properties that block Player 4 from completing his pink or yellow monopolies. Player 4 can easily pay the rent from one house on dark blue, so that threat is not enough to force him out.

Player 3 cannot build more on dark blue. Two houses there would cost $400, but they only have $397 and must pay a $50 jail fee. Brown hotels are also too cheap to threaten Player 4. No opponent can currently force him out.

Player 4 is winning by attrition through light blue hotels. I am now considering selling the orange monopoly to Player 3 in exchange for dark blue or cash, hoping Player 3 could build on it and threaten Player 4.

Selling the orange monopoly to Player 3 would still leave me exposed, since I would continue landing on those spaces. Trading away the pink properties would also be suicidal, because the recipient could flip them to Player 4. I am now weighing whether to propose a trade to Player 3 that offers nothing dangerous, and I am checking if rejecting a trade proposal gives me another decision.

Rejected trade proposals may return as follow-up decisions, but offering a bad deal wastes time and signals desperation. I cannot trade with both Player 2 and Player 3 simultaneously. Player 4 will not give up Kentucky, and I do not want to pay him for it. I will not mortgage any properties now; the seventy-seven dollars in cash is enough liquidity for survival.

No trade improves both survival and win chance. Funding Player 3 to build dark blue houses would hurt me too, since I still land on Boardwalk and Park Place. Player 2 cannot threaten Player 4. The best play is to end the turn, hold blockers, and avoid pre-mortgaging or trading away Marvin Gardens, the pink properties, or anything to Player 4. I will warn other players not to trade with Player 4.

message.reasoning:
I need to make a decision in this Monopoly turn.

Analyzing the game state. I have $77 cash and my position shows JAIL but in_jail is false. This appears to be a post-turn action decision.

I have the orange monopoly but New York Avenue is mortgaged. I also own Water Works and Marvin Gardens. I am weighing whether to mortgage a property, propose a trade, or end my turn.

p2 has $540 and is weak. p3 has $397, is in jail, and owns hotels on the dark blue set plus mortgaged railroads and utilities.

p4 has $3251 and owns light blue hotels, the pink set, and several railroads. They lack the pink and yellow monopolies that I hold.

I will keep Marvin Gardens and the pink properties to avoid completing monopolies for p4. I cannot unmortgage any properties right now.

I cannot unmortgage New York Avenue because it costs $110 and I only have $77. I will not mortgage properties preemptively. I am checking standard mortgage values for my other holdings.

Mortgaging all six properties would raise $535, bringing total cash to $612. That covers a $600 hotel hit. Pre-mortgaging would sacrifice rent income and future interest payments. I am now considering whether to trade.

I cannot build on the orange monopoly because I lack the $110 to unmortgage New York Avenue and the $77 cash to buy houses. I am now considering trading with p3 or p2 to raise cash, since p3 has $397 and is in jail.

Selling Marvin Gardens to p2 would not complete a monopoly for them. Selling it to p4 would complete the yellow set and severely damage my position. I will not trade away any orange monopoly pieces.

I am now calculating the exact rent I would pay if I roll a 4 from Jail and land on Virginia. I also noted that p3 could flip any pink properties I trade to them toward p4.

Rolling from Jail is mostly safe. Virginia costs $12, Pennsylvania RR costs $50, and New York Avenue is mortgaged so it collects no rent. I am now looking for a trade that improves my position.

Developing the orange monopoly is impossible with only $77. It would require roughly $1,600 to unmortgage New York Avenue and build hotels. p4 has the cash but will not fund my development. p2 and p3 together cannot afford it either.

I cannot complete the red or green monopolies. p3 owns Indiana and Illinois, but they are mortgaged, and p4 holds Kentucky. The green set is split three ways. p4 holds three of the four yellow properties and will never sell one to me.

I rejected trading my pink properties to p4 because that would complete their pink monopoly and fund the leader. I also dismissed bankrupting p4 as unrealistic.

Instead, I am now considering selling Water Works to p2 for cash. This would let me unmortgage New York Avenue, which costs $110 and is currently blocking my orange development.

I rejected the Water Works trade. It would not raise enough cash to develop the orange monopoly meaningfully, and a utility monopoly would only slightly hurt me when I land there.

I also decided against selling anything to p3 for cash. Pre-selling would reduce my rent income, and p3 is unlikely to go broke from light blue hotels right now.

The correct play is to end my turn. I will not pre-mortgage, sell blockers, or fund p4.
